observations: Top view of a matte black game console, design matches a PlayStation 4 Slim.
Two boxed DualShock 4 controllers are placed behind the console.
The console surface shows some light scuffing and dust.
A watermark 'DERA NWOYE' is visible across the image.

claims.evidence: No photo of the system software version or the game library on screen.

claims.claim: comes with two brand new pads
claims.evidence: Boxes are shown, but the controllers inside are not visible and authenticity cannot be confirmed.
Photo 0 shows the console in generally good cosmetic condition, despite minor scuffs.
The warranty seals on the rear of the console are not shown.
The seller also claims the pads are 'brand new' in boxes; original pads would be the ones packaged with the console at first sale, not new replacements.
The receipt is mentioned but not pictured.

risks.risk: The console may not be on a hackable firmware (9.00 or lower).
risks.proof: A photo of the 'System Information' screen showing the 'System Software' version.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a standard unhacked console

risks.risk: The console may have been opened or repaired.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the back of the console showing intact warranty stickers.

risks.risk: The 'brand new' controllers may be third-party clones rather than genuine Sony products.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the labels on the back of the controllers.

risks.risk: The console might have internal faults like overheating or a faulty HDMI port.
risks.proof: A video showing the console booting up and running a demanding game for several minutes.

proof_requests: Photo of the System Information screen showing the firmware version.
Photo of the back of the console showing the warranty seals.
Photo of the back of the controllers to verify authenticity.
Video of the console running a game to prove it doesn't overheat.
Photo of the UK receipt mentioned in the description.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a PS4 Slim. While many claims are unverified, it can be priced at its worst-case value (unhacked, potentially repaired, with generic controllers).
